Got the chance of running the examples and glance over the code... it looks incredibly elegant and clean. Almost feels like this could make engine development fun again.
MIT License, well done! It's so refreshing to see things released with no strings attached... a breathe of fresh air as a potential end user.
I have to say the API seems to be very pleasant and simple at a glance. Kudos to the author! This pattern is a great example of how Rust achieves to be both very ergonomic and type safe.
This is amazing. Seriously: I had a look at nearly every game engine/GUI solution in Rust and this is by far the most thought out, ergonomic and complete thing I found.

Having spent a good deal of time working in a dogmatic data driven entity component system very similar to this one, I'd like to point out that while it's very aesthetically pleasing to write code like that, it's not necessarily more productive.
I'm getting security warnings visiting the site, on both Firefox and Chrome... 'Error code: SEC_ERROR_UNKNOWN_ISSUER' on FF at least.
AAA studios won't even consider using Bevy until it has more features and has stood the test of time. So in the short term our market is essentially 'indies and enthusiasts'.
The integrated code editor in Godot is actually something I don't like... I hope that Bevy users won't be forced to use the Bevy editor for coding.
Bevy's release notes are consistently the best I've ever seen.
We support low-end devices well! Bevy runs well on iOS currently... Fans spinning is a known issue, but it is generally decoupled from framerates.
Not a criticism, but model projected shadows are very jagged or really low-res, reminds me of early Unity shadows.
Things have started to stabilize, but unless you're willing to get your hands dirty and deal with regular breaking changes, I don't yet recommend staking your livelihood on it.
On the last update 0.10 -> 0.11, I had to make quite a few changes on my app, but this time it compiled out of the box!
I'm put off by the limited docs. I've read the Bevy book, only takes a few minutes, and just like that I'm out of resources to turn to when I get stuck.
There's an unofficial complement to the docs... Unfortunately it's somewhat out of date... The effort to keep it up to date is somewhat low since Bevy changes so much and so often.

Pain points: UI system was too verbose to comfortably build widgets. Swapped to using egui, but expect to go back to native Bevy within a year. egui has significant limitations, too. Parent/Child relationships don't have a ton of support.

Pros: Very nice to work in Rust engine + Rust game. Once you get your brain thinking ECS it's tough to go back, feels very flexible. Very lively community, easy to find someone to talk to about a problem you're having.
Bevy is one of my favorite game engines, especially for larger projects. Asset V2 preprocessing and .meta files look super useful.
Something delightful about this update: it has a lot of new features, some very early, but all by different authors. Seems like such a community effort compared to most early-stage projects.
Man, you guys really kill it with blog/changelog announcements. Great job! For my use case, Bevy web (and mobile is nice too) support would mean switching from Godot, 100%.
